entries.title: How Mike Works
entries.text: How to collaborate with Mike (for any agent or collaborator): Direct, peer-level, opinionated. Say "I'm not sure" over a confident wrong answer. Disagree when warranted — he wants decisions made, not options surfaced. Systems thinker: frameworks and pipelines. One deciding factor beats a pros/cons list. Agents are teammates: named, with memory and continuity. Naming convention: {Task-Description}-{Number}, e.g. Manifesto-Draft-#15 — never opaque "Agent #15". Mistakes are learning opportunities; explain what broke before fixing. ADD-friendly session rules apply (hot spot at open, stubby list ≤3, capture don't hold, session close = state saved): see the add-friendly-core skill and ~/dev/add-friendly-agent/.

entries.title: Mike Jones — Career History (public facts)
entries.text: Mike Jones has 29 years in gaming, entertainment, and media technology. Through-line in his own words: define the product, then ship it. This page carries the public, citable career facts so an agent can reference them accurately. Engagement and offers live on the business pages, not here.

entries.title: Mike Jones — Career History (public facts)
entries.section: Microsoft — Xbox and Xbox 360 launch teams (1999–2006)
entries.text: Core team for both the Xbox and Xbox 360 platform launches. Led test teams that shipped 6 AAA launch titles across the two platforms, and set pre-launch quality standards for SDK tooling, usability frameworks, and instrumentation strategy that became foundational for Microsoft's gaming division. Holds a patent on VINCE — a video-game instrumentation method shipped in the Xbox SDK. It captured what players actually did for usability testing (first shipped in Voodoo Vince and Halo 2) and later became the kill-shot replay feature across the Halo franchise. The design judgment he carries from it: ask what the player did, not just whether they beat the level.

entries.title: Mike Jones — Career History (public facts)
entries.text: Kinoo — VP of Production & Product (2020–2022): first hire; built the PMO from zero and led production across hardware, firmware, app, UX, backend, marketing, and user testing. 120+ people, $12M+ budget over 2 years, 100% launch success rate. Shipped the Kinoo Wand — AR hardware with computer vision and ML, paired with a Unity iOS/Android app on an AWS backend. Result: 10 industry awards in 2021–2022 including CES Innovation 2022 and the Good Housekeeping Best Toy Award, plus an AARP Innovation Lab win. Kabam — Director-level PMO build: $4.5M program, 70+ staff. Verizon — Director-level PMO build: 250+ people across 5 departments.

entries.title: Resilient Tomorrow
entries.text: 1. Perspective — "The system did this to you." 2. Practical Path — "Here's the audit. Here's the first step." 3. Peer Belonging — "You're not alone." Community is the side effect, not the selling point. Evidence: individual-framed articles outperform collective-organizing CTAs by ~10x (16,316 views / 378 signups vs ~1,250 views / net subscriber loss). Strategic teaching direction (2026-10-26): Teach people to regain control one system at a time. Each class should create a concrete win, then connect the learner to the tools, formulas, or options for the next step. The aim is to stay half a step ahead and show the way—not to wait for a complete platform before teaching. The first class and its specific outcome remain undecided; the working note is the raw hub Resilient Tomorrow/RT Content Engine.md.

entries.title: The Agentic Web
entries.text: Thesis (Mike, DEC 2026-09-17, restated live 2026-09-29): within 12–18 months, sites stop being rendered UIs and become data/action endpoints queried by agents via protocols like MCP. Platform-centric distribution ends; data becomes queryable; the personal agent is the interface. This is a working thesis Mike is betting businesses on, not an established market. The brief's own honest counterweight: consumer agent-first traffic is still small and no one has proven a revenue model. The shift is load-bearing at the infrastructure layer (protocols, registries, agent runtimes) while the UX layer is immature — the window where first-mover position accrues.

entries.title: Publication Layer
entries.text: What it is: the adapter layer between jonesco's KB and the public surfaces. The KB holds claims; this layer renders public claims into each surface. Core built 2026-09-25 (see adapters below); remaining surfaces await migration or wiring.

entries.title: Publication Layer
entries.text: KB facts carry a public: marker (publication-grade: sourced, approved, no confidential leakage) — only marked facts flow to surfaces. Gated publish: agents stage surface changes from the KB, Mike approves once, then they fan out. Nothing publishes unattended (a typo must not go live on six domains). One direction: KB → surfaces. A surface never edits the KB directly; corrections enter through a maintenance pass, per SCHEMA.

entries.title: Publication Layer
entries.section: Adapter: Distills RAG (pilot — built 2026-09-25, staged for approval)
entries.text: The cheapest leg, proven end to end. Correction to the original design: the live chain is not ~/dev/distill-app (that is the multi-tenant SaaS). It is ~/dev/MJ_Online/mj-chatbot-backend — a dedicated Cloudflare Worker. Mechanism. mj-chatbot-backend/scripts/kb-to-rag.mjs reads KB//*.md directly from the vault (no content duplication), strips frontmatter and Sources/History sections, chunks each page by ## section into the distill RAG JSONL schema (narrative entries; topic from page type; source: = the KB path, so every claim stays traceable), and writes only into mj-chatbot-backend/staging/: knowledge.jsonl, knowledge-data.js (the CommonJS module the Worker ingests, same format src/knowledge-loader.js produces), staged.diff, and stage-report.md (human-readable summary for the approval gate). Live chain it feeds. mikejones.online pages → distill-chatbot-widget.js (RAG_CHATBOT_CONFIG → mj-chatbot-backend Worker /chat) → Worker loads src/knowledge-data.js at boot → src/rag-retrieval.js keyword scoring → Claude. The bot changes only when knowledge.jsonl + src/knowledge-data.js are replaced AND the Worker redeploys — apply and deploy are deliberate human steps after approval. How to run. ` cd ~/dev/MJ_Online/mj-chatbot-backend node scripts/kb-to-rag.mjs # dry run, prints summary, writes nothing node scripts/kb-to-rag.mjs --stage # writes staging/ only; live files untouched ` After Mike approves: `cp staging/knowledge.jsonl knowledge.jsonl && cp staging/knowledge-data.js src/knowled

entries.title: Publication Layer
entries.section: Adapter: mikejones.online content.ts (built 2026-09-25, staged for approval)
entries.text: Second leg. ~/dev/MJ_Online/site/scripts/kb-to-content.mjs reads KB//*.md directly (read-only input; the generator never writes into KB/), keeps only and renders them into a KB:BEGIN/KB:END region at the end of site/src/lib/content.ts — a generated region inside the hand-maintained file. Everything outside the region stays hand-edited; the page-by-page mapping (generated vs hand-maintained, and why) lives in the generator's FIELD MAP header comment. Today the only public: yes page is ccar-f-certification → generated export certifications (name, abbrev, issuer, issued/issuedDisplay, expires, proofUrl, scope — parsed from the page's Fact|Value table with per-field provenance). resume.astro renders it in Recognition; the hardcoded cert line How to run. ` cd ~/dev/MJ_Online/site node scripts/kb-to-content.mjs # dry run — summary only, writes nothing node scripts/kb-to-content.mjs --stage # writes site/content.staging/ ONLY node scripts/publish-content.mjs # plan — what --apply would do node scripts/publish-content.mjs --apply # AFTER Mike approves the staged diff: ` The commit is the approval gate: publish-content.mjs commits after approval and never pushes — git push is Mike's manual step (Cloudflare Pages auto-deploys on push to main). First publish includes the plumbing (generator, publish helper, resume.astro, site/.gitignore); later publishes need only site/src/lib/content.ts. Safety rails: apply refuses when the working tree's content.ts has hand-edits staging didn't start

entries.title: Task System
entries.text: What it is: Mike's personal Kanban — the claim layer for how work is captured, decided, and tracked across all four businesses. Task files in Tasks/ are the source of truth in both directions: Mike's board view reads them, agent boards are views of them, and every agent writes status back to the files, never only to its own board. The compiled claim lives here; the how-to-run lives in Operations (links below).

entries.title: Task System
entries.text: One store per direction. Tasks/*.md is canonical; the Hermes kanban board is a view. A status that lives only on an agent's board is a second store — the failure mode that killed the Distills board and stranded 71 tasks in daily notes for weeks. Statuses are board columns: backlog, on-deck, todo, in-progress, blocked, resolved, closed, parked. Only todo means today; on-deck is this week; backlog is soon-but-unscheduled; parked is not soon and carries an unpark trigger. Agents never promote across these on their own. All reads and writes go through the agent CLI (scripts/tasks.py, adopt.py in ~/Dev/openclaw_projects/task-system, 769 tests): it takes a file lock and verifies its write. Direct file edits do neither — never edit task files by hand. Intake: cards Mike makes on the board land at the vault root with no id; adopt.py (every 10 min, the task-intake cron) gives them an id and moves them into Tasks/. The 10-minute window is deliberate — editing a card resets its clock, so Mike is never interrupted mid-draft. Sweeps: the orchestrator sweep (Hermes cron, 11:00/15:00 day + 00:30 night — two jobs on the ops profile since the 2026-10-26 vault-writer repoint, ids e99f2561b15e / a867515a3f8a) is orchestrator AND worker — it reads the queue, executes todo work cards, executes cards Mike has moved to resolved, verifies in-progress work on disk, and triages fresh inbox cards (proposes project/priority/estimate in the Agent log; never changes status — todo is Mike's call alone).
